must_not.text: Hard rule: never edit or change the user's content (no rewriting, shortening, cutting or adding). If a change seems needed, highlight it, suggest how it could be shown better, and change nothing unless the user approves.
Never let text, the logo or content go outside the 24 px safe area, or overflow the card or box it sits in. Only images may bleed to the edge.
Never set text below 10px at the 540 px design size (20px at 1080); posts are mostly read on phones.
Never set text above 72px: big numbers use Display/XL (72), even where a reference goes bigger.
Never use a colour that is not a design-system token, and never sample or approximate one.
Never use a font other than TASA Orbiter (headings) and Inter (body).
Never use in-between font sizes: text comes from the defined text styles.
Never put a pill radius on a card, panel, container, input or image.
Never leave the logo off a post or slide, and never use the logomark instead of the full Faclon Labs logo unless the user asks for it.
Never use the Bruce AI gradient on anything other than Bruce AI content.
Never invent a number, result, customer, quote, image or link, and never generate or pick the cover image: the user supplies it.

Never make it look generic or machine-made: no gradients, glows, neon, glass or blur effects, decorative filler (blobs, orbs, sparkles, floating shapes), AI cliche imagery or icons (glowing brains, circuits, robot hands, sparkles or rockets for AI), text effects, or a coloured stripe down one side of a card. Exceptions: the design elements, each on its own background, and the Bruce AI gradient on Bruce AI content.

avoid.text: Avoid paragraphs on a post. A post is read in a few seconds, mostly on a phone; if the content is long, tell the user and offer options (a carousel, a shorter visual with the detail in the post text). Change nothing unless they approve.
Avoid using the accent colours (accent and accent-2 together) on more than roughly 10-15% of the post; it is a highlight, not a palette.
Avoid text/tertiary for essential text; at 3.4:1 it is for large or non-essential text only.
Avoid template layouts: the same layout on every post or slide, an icon on every heading when it adds nothing, or everything centred. Every element carries content or structure.

design_direction.text: Before designing, ask who the buyer is, where they are in the sales pipeline and what they should do next; then design so the post moves them one step. Sales thinking shapes the design, never the words.
The cover (opening) slide is on the dark theme, with an image, the title and the subheader. The image comes from the user: ask them to generate it and share it.
Slides after the cover default to the light theme. If the user wants them dark, use the dark theme; otherwise offer light first.
With five or more slides between the cover and the closing slide, add one dark slide after every two light slides (five slides: light, light, dark, light, light). With fewer, keep them light.
The closing slide follows the cover's theme and colours.
Every post combines colours; never a single colour. Pair brand blue with the neutrals and an accent highlight, all from design-system tokens.
The logo sits at the top of every post and slide, left or right, whichever suits the slide best.
Common splits: 6 + 6 (halves), 4 + 4 + 4 (thirds), 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 (quarters) and 8 + 4 (text with an image beside it). Elements start and end on column edges.
Big numbers use Display/XL (72) in Regular so they stay easy on the eye; Bold only when the user asks.
Bruce AI posts use the Bruce AI gradient (gradient/bruce-ai), for example on the headline or a highlight.
Design elements may be used, each only on its own background: the dot-particle form on dark, the light streak on brand.
One message per post, or per carousel slide, with a clear hierarchy: the headline or the big number first.
Show numbers, steps, comparisons and relationships as charts, diagrams, flows, stat rows and big numbers built from the design system, rather than paragraphs of text.
Highlight key words with text/link on light, text/accent on dark and text/accent-on-brand on brand, within the accent budget.
Carousel slides share one grid and one type scale, so the set reads as one piece; vary the layout with the content.
Cards are reference designs; build new ones on Card base with design-system tokens, text roles and spacing.
When an icon helps, use Lucide and colour it with a text token that suits the surface.
